questions: Q1: What CLI changes are needed for hlx inspect netsuite?
Q2: What CLI changes are needed for the new hlx run top-level command?
Q3: How do the new commands interact with existing auth/HTTP infrastructure?
Q4: Does the CLI need an --env flag or is environment purely token-bounded?

answers.answer: Add 'netsuite' case in src/inspect/index.ts switch (after 'api' case at L109). Create src/inspect/netsuite.ts following the db.ts 12-line template: resolveRepo -> hxFetch POST to /{repoId}/netsuite with body -> JSON output. Add help text in inspectUsage() at L9-31. For SuiteQL queries, the handler takes a query string (positional or --query-file). For NS script logs, the same endpoint may accept a --logs flag or a type discriminator in the body. The --query-file flag handling already exists in the router (lines 70-88) and extends naturally to the netsuite case.

src/inspect/db.ts:5-12 -- 12-line handler template: resolveRepo -> hxFetch POST /{repoId}/database -> console.log
src/inspect/index.ts:9-31 -- inspectUsage function with help text

answers.answer: Add 'run' case in src/index.ts top-level switch (L81-156, after 'inspect' case at L90). Create src/run/index.ts as a new handler module (src/run/ directory does not exist). The command takes: (a) a script via inline code or --script-file flag, (b) a --repo flag for org context/audit attribution, (c) optional --modules flag listing NetSuite module IDs. Uses hxFetch POST with body { code, modules? }. May need basePath override to '/api/inspect' or '/api' depending on server route. May need longer timeout than 30s REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS since SuiteScript execution can be slow. Add help text in usage() at L37-67.

src/lib/http.ts:43 -- basePath defaults to /api/inspect, supports override via options.basePath

answers.answer: Both commands use the existing hxFetch client (http.ts:37-134) with its dual-mode auth: hxi_ tokens -> X-API-Key header, other -> Authorization: Bearer header. Config loaded from env vars (HELIX_API_KEY > HELIX_INSPECT_TOKEN > HELIX_INSPECT_API_KEY per config.ts:42). In sandbox agent context, HELIX_INSPECT_TOKEN is set by the orchestrator's configureInspectionForStep and contains the nsEnv claim. The CLI does not parse or inspect nsEnv -- the server extracts it from the token. resolveRepo is used for repo context. The 3-attempt retry with exponential backoff applies to both commands.

src/lib/config.ts:42-43 -- env var priority: HELIX_API_KEY > HELIX_INSPECT_TOKEN > HELIX_INSPECT_API_KEY
src/lib/http.ts:64-130 -- fetch with retry logic (3 attempts, exponential backoff)

answers.answer: Environment is TOKEN-BOUNDED. The nsEnv claim is set at token issuance time by the orchestrator based on workflow step (scout/diagnosis=PRODUCTION, else=SANDBOX). The CLI does NOT need an --env flag for sandbox agents -- the token already encodes the allowed environment. For human users with hxi_ API keys, an --env query parameter may be supported server-side as a future consideration, but the initial implementation should not add a CLI-side --env flag. The continuation context confirms: 'the CLI may select env only within what the token authorizes; per-step default routing stays'.
evidence: Continuation context: nsEnv is a TOKEN-BOUNDED flag
session.ts:102-112 -- Token claims set at issuance; scope and nsEnv baked in
src/lib/config.ts:42-45 -- HELIX_INSPECT_TOKEN env var used by sandbox agents; token carries all claims
credentials.ts:9-14 -- scout/diagnosis -> PRODUCTION, else -> SANDBOX routing preserved in token

statement: The helix-cli needs two new commands matching the two-surface governance model: (1) 'hlx inspect netsuite' as a new case in the inspect router following the established db.ts handler pattern (~12 lines), routing SuiteQL queries and script log requests through the server-side proxy, and (2) 'hlx run' as a new top-level command for arbitrary SuiteScript execution. Both use the existing hxFetch HTTP client with dual-mode auth and retry logic. Environment routing is purely token-bounded -- no --env flag required. The implementation is low-risk: small additions following verified patterns with no modifications to existing handlers. Changes are confined to: src/index.ts (add run case + usage text), src/inspect/index.ts (add netsuite case + usage text), and two new handler files (src/inspect/netsuite.ts, src/run/index.ts). Zero new runtime dependencies.
